skills.name: Writing a paragraph about a bus journey

note.text:
A paragraph is a group of sentences about one main idea. It starts on a new line.
• The topic sentence comes first and says what the paragraph is about: “Last December I travelled from Kumba to Douala by bus.”
• The supporting sentences give the details in order: buying the ticket, the departure, what happened on the way, the arrival.
• Use sequence words: first, then, after that, later, finally.
• A story about the past is in the Simple Past: I went, I bought, the bus left, we arrived.
• The last sentence closes the paragraph, for example with how you felt.

worked_example.problem: Plan a paragraph about a bus journey from {t} to {d}.
steps: Topic sentence: Last December I travelled from {t} to {d} by bus.
Details in order, with sequence words: First I bought my ticket. Then the bus left. After that we stopped at a checkpoint.
Closing sentence: Finally we arrived, and I was happy to see my cousins.
worked_example.answer: Topic sentence → details in order (first, then, after that) → closing sentence, all in the Simple Past.

cards.idea: A paragraph starts with a topic sentence that says what it is about.
example: Topic sentence: “Last holiday I travelled to Bafoussam by bus.”
Not a topic sentence: “Then we stopped for food.” (a detail)

pick.r: Last holiday I travelled from Buea to Bamenda by bus.
e: That is a detail in the middle.
That is not about the journey.
pick.y: It says what the whole paragraph is about.

pick.r: My journey to Kribi by bus was long but exciting.
e: That is about the town, not the journey.
pick.y: It names the journey and gives the main idea.

pick.r: Last month my family took a bus from Limbe to Yaoundé.
w: I was very tired at the end.
e: That is the first detail, not the topic.
That is not about the journey.
pick.y: It tells who travelled, where and how.

check.prompt: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about a bus journey?

cards.idea: Sequence words show the order of events: first, then, after that, later, finally.
example: First I bought a ticket. Then I found a seat.
After that the bus left. Finally we arrived.

cards.idea: A story about a past journey is in the Simple Past.
example: I {past('go')} to the motor park and {past('buy')} a ticket.
The bus {past('leave')} at eight and we {past('arrive')} at noon.

check.prompt: Write the verb in the Simple Past.
check.text: Last week we ___ to Limbe by bus. ({v})

misconceptions.explain: The journey was last week: use the past, {past(v)}.

questions.prompt: Put the sentences of the paragraph in order.

items.text: Last Saturday I travelled to Bamenda by bus
First I bought my ticket at the agency
Then the conductor loaded my bag
After that the bus left the park
Finally we arrived in the afternoon

paper_task.prompt: Write one paragraph (six to eight sentences) in your exercise book about a journey you made by bus. Start with a topic sentence, give the events in order with sequence words, use the Simple Past, and end with how you felt.
model: Last December I travelled from Kumba to Douala by bus. First my father took me to the motor park and bought my ticket. Then the conductor put my bag on the roof and I found a seat by the window. After that the bus left, and I watched the plantations go past. On the way we stopped at a checkpoint, and later at a market where I bought groundnuts. Finally we arrived in Douala in the evening. I was tired, but I was happy to see my cousins waiting for me.
checklist: My paragraph starts with a topic sentence.
The events are in the order they happened.
I used sequence words (first, then, after that, finally).
My verbs are in the Simple Past.
I wrote by bus, by taxi (not by the bus).
My last sentence closes the paragraph.
Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
